text.p: The following are the leading stories in the local press on Tuesday, May 6. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Traditional leaders in Chikwawa, more than 40 km south of the main commercial city Blantyre are divided over whether to agree with government's decision to disposess former president Kamuzu Banda of his 5,600-hectare ranch.

- Malawi Congress of Trade Unions (MCTU) president Ken Mhango urged government on Monday to convene a meeting of all labour unions in the civil service -- instead of meeting them separately -- to resolve problems leading to the strike now in its fifth week.

- As the Customs Workers Union (CWU) prepares to join the strike in sympathy with civil servants on Tuesday, government has bowed down to pressure to resume negotiations with the workers to implement in full recommendations of an independent commission of inquiry.

- Main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) vice president Gwanda Chakuamba swore at a rally that his party would resist government's move to snatch the 5,600-hectare ranch from former president Kamuzu Banda.

- Cabinet has recommended that President Bakili Muluzi be restrained from making premature public statements about projects that the government would be implementing after he announced that civil servants would receive wage increases in full as recommended by an independent commission of inquiry.
- Striking civil servants in Northern Malawi have resorted to violence and clashed with police who fired 45 teargass cannisters and five live bullets into the protesting crowds.
